summary: This joint resolution nullifies the Department of Labor's October 2025 rule setting the Adverse Effect Wage Rate methodology for H-2A agricultural guest workers by declaring it has no force or effect.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a Congressional Review Act resolution disapproving a specific DOL regulatory methodology for wage rates in the H-2A program. It contains no provisions that authorize, appropriate, or alter any government expenditures.
The bill addresses only the validity of a DOL wage-rate rule for H-2A visas and has no tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures.
No healthcare coverage, insurance, or medical-service provisions appear in the bill.
The bill is silent on firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.

The bill directly targets the Department of Labor rule that sets the Adverse Effect Wage Rate methodology for H-2A temporary agricultural workers. Because H-2A is an immigration visa category, disapproving the wage-rate rule alters the terms under which foreign workers may be admitted, giving the measure a clear, albeit narrow, connection to immigration policy.
No abortion-related language or reproductive-health provisions are present.
The bill contains nothing concerning military or defense spending.
No environmental, climate, or regulatory provisions on emissions or natural resources are included.
The bill does not address welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.
No education funding, school-choice, or federal-education-policy language exists.
The bill is unrelated to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
No criminal-sentencing, policing, or justice-reform measures are present.
The bill does not alter tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export rules.
No deficit, debt-ceiling, or fiscal-balance provisions appear.
The bill contains no LGBTQ-related civil-rights or nondiscrimination language.
No foreign-assistance funding or policy changes are involved.
The bill is silent on voting access, election administration, or voter-ID requirements.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance provisions exist.

The bill concerns the wage-rate methodology that governs H-2A agricultural guest workers—an issue that directly affects wage floors and labor-market protections for both domestic and foreign farm labor. While not about union organizing per se, the measure engages labor-market regulation at a moderate level.
No religious-exemption or civil-rights-balancing language is present.
